items.title: Sjögren's Disease With Primary Biliary Cholangitis Fulfilling the 2010 ACR/EULAR Classification Criteria for Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Case Report and Review of an Under-Recognized Overlap.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) and primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) are chronic autoimmune epithelitides that target exocrine glands and small intrahepatic bile ducts, respectively. Their coexistence is well described; less appreciated is a specific and avoidable failure mode. Because rheumatoid factor (RF) positivity, symmetric small-joint involvement and elevated acute-phase reactants are all common in SjD, patients with SjD-associated polyarthritis may reach the six-point threshold of the 2010 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism (ACR/EULAR) classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis (RA); those criteria remain valid only if their mandatory exclusion clause is applied. We report a 49-year-old woman who carried a three-year diagnosis of RF-positive, anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA)-negative RA and had been treated with methotrexate and tofacitinib without ever developing radiographic erosions. Cholestatic liver injury during a course of amoxicillin-clavulanate led to the detection of anti-mitochondrial M2 antibodies and to a liver biopsy showing florid duct lesions with periductal granulomas, establishing stage 1 PBC. Directed questioning subsequently revealed a three-year history of previously unreported sicca symptoms. Anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen A autoantibodies (anti-Ro/SSA) were positive, the Schirmer test measured 1 mm bilaterally, and minor salivary gland biopsy demonstrated focal lymphocytic sialadenitis with a focus score of 2. These findings yielded a total of 7/9 points according to the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for SjD, with relevant exclusion criteria assessed and found to be absent. Immunosuppression was withdrawn, followed by sustained biochemical and articular improvement over 24 months after initiation of ursodeoxycholic acid and hydroxychloroquine. We review the epidemiology, shared immunopathogenesis, and therapeutic implications of the SjD-PBC overlap, and propose that, in an appropriate clinical context, a structured inquiry into sicca symptoms and consideration of anti-Ro/SSA testing may be useful in patients with ACPA-negative, RF-positive, non-erosive polyarthritis before escalation to biologic or targeted synthetic therapy.

items.title: Listeria monocytogenes Sepsis With Meningitis Complicating Biologic Immunosuppression in a Patient With Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Secondary to Adult-Onset Still's Disease: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) are treated with potent immunosuppression, including high-dose corticosteroids and biologic agents such as anakinra, which can result in an increased risk of opportunistic infections such as listeriosis (infection with Listeria monocytogenes  (L.  monocytogenes )). This case report describes a 34-year-old man on a background of AOSD receiving escalated doses of steroids and anakinra for a probable flare-up of HLH. Whilst inpatient, he developed high-grade pyrexia (39.3°C), acute confusion, and neurological deterioration, requiring admission to the ICU for intubation and ventilatory support. Investigations revealed blood cultures positive for L. monocytogenes , and lumbar puncture findings were consistent with acute bacterial meningitis. The patient clinically improved with targeted antimicrobial therapy and was successfully extubated, with subsequent normalisation of his inflammatory markers. He was discharged with a planned taper of his immunosuppressive therapy. This case emphasises the synergistic risk of infection associated with biologic therapy and high-dose corticosteroid use and the importance of maintaining a low threshold for considering listeriosis in immunocompromised patients, particularly in the presence of neurological deterioration.

items.title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in a Young Man: A Multisystemic Diagnostic Challenge.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex, phenotypically varied disorder that possesses wide-ranging cardiac involvement. Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is one such cardiac manifestation, which results from the deposition of verrucous, sessile lesions favoring the left-sided heart valves. LSE is typically clinically silent without significant valvular dysfunction. Such patients with LSE, however, are those most susceptible to a more severe clinical phenotype resulting from SLE. Here, we report a unique case of a 22-year-old man initially presenting with unilateral leg swelling found to be secondary to a deep-vein thrombosis. He subsequently developed a constellation of acute symptoms, including embolic strokes, splenic infarction, proteinuric kidney injury, and significant mitral regurgitation, all of which mimicked bacterial endocarditis. His complex, multi-systemic disease course presented diagnostic challenges. We highlight the need in such complex cases for a specialist-led multidisciplinary approach, including cardiologists and rheumatologists, to guide serological and radiological investigations. Early use of echocardiography, in particular 3D transesophageal imaging, was paramount in clinching the diagnosis of LSE as an index presentation of SLE and in the transition from intravenous antibiotics to immunosuppression. Our case underscores the importance of the multidisciplinary team and the role of echocardiography in identifying such patients with LSE in SLE and thereby those most vulnerable to significant end-organ sequelae.

items.title: Predicting infection risk in rheumatoid arthritis patients receiving biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs: an application of machine learning and healthcare big data.
items.abstract: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) initiating biologic or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/ts DMARDs) face elevated risk of serious infections, necessitating tools for individualized risk stratification. Primary objective was to develop and validate a clinically interpretable machine learning (ML) model to predict 1-year risk of serious infection after b/ts DMARD initiation; secondary objectives were to estimate infection incidence and identify key predictors associated with risk. We performed a retrospective cohort study using territory-wide EHR from Hong Kong's Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) for model development and internal validation, with external validation in the U.S. All of Us database. The outcome was first serious infection requiring hospitalization within 1 year. Candidate predictors included demographics, comorbidities, prior infections and medications, laboratory markers. Multiple ML algorithms were trained; model selection was based on AUROC, and interpretability was assessed using SHAP. A total of 3,159 patients from CDARS (8.8% with serious infections) and 1,845 from All of Us (2.8% with serious infections) were included. The model demonstrated the highest AUROC in internal validation (0.840, 95% CI: 0.793-0.888) and maintained robust performance in external validation (AUROC: 0.729, 95% CI: 0.665-0.793). Key predictors included prior infections, diabetes, b/ts DMARD type, and inflammatory markers. Rituximab was linked to the highest infection risk, while tofacitinib and upadacitinib had the lowest. This study developed and validated an ML model using routine clinical data to predict serious infection risk in RA patients, supporting personalised treatment and proactive infection management. items.title: Cardiometabolic and Nutritional Parameters in Patients with Primary Sjögren Syndrome.
items.abstract: Primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease of the exocrine glands that may contribute to altered nutritional status. The aim of this study was to investigate the association between pSS and various nutritional and cardiometabolic parameters. This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 91 patients with pSS and 100 healthy controls. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed, including serum levels of albumin, glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), lipids, 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], and other biomarkers. Principal component analysis was applied to reduce the number of variables and identify key factors associated with pSS. Body mass index (BMI) and serum concentrations of albumin, glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol were significantly lower in patients with pSS than in controls (p=0.001, p<0.001, p=0.013, p=0.035, p=0.010, and p=0.001, respectively). Serum 25(OH)D levels were significantly higher in the pSS group compared with controls (p<0.001). Multivariable binary logistic regression analysis showed that BMI and 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with pSS (p=0.013 and p<0.001, respectively). Of the five factors extracted by factor analysis, three were significantly associated with pSS. The factor including CRP, HbA1c, and BMI and the factor including albumin and LDL cholesterol were negatively associated with pSS, whereas the factor comprising 25(OH)D and vitamin B12 was positively associated with pSS. Lower BMI and higher serum 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with pSS. Combined factors related to inflammation, glycemic status, lipid metabolism, and nutritional markers showed distinct associations with pSS, highlighting the importance of nutritional status screening in these patients.

items.title: Does Takayasu arteritis differ between children and adolescents? Insights from a Russian multicenter cohort.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a chronic large-vessel vasculitis with significant age-related heterogeneity. Global data highlight differences between adult and pediatric TA, as well as among different pediatric age groups. However, the epidemiology and clinical features of childhood-onset TA in the Russian population are largely unknown. To characterize the clinical and laboratory features, age-related differences, and long-term outcomes of TA in a Russian pediatric cohort. A retrospective multicenter cohort study included 79 patients aged under 18 years with TA, diagnosed according to EULAR/PRINTO/PRES criteria, from four centers in the Russian Federation. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and instrumental data were collected. Patients were stratified into two age groups according to WHO definitions: Children (aged less than 10 years, n = 25) and adolescents (aged 10 years to 17 years inclusive, n = 54). Disease activity was assessed using ITAS2010 and ITAS.A. Statistical analysis was performed using StatTech v.4.12.2. The median age at onset was 11.0 (8.0-14.0) years, and the time before diagnosis was 8.0 (2.0-17.5) months; females were 78.5%. The most common clinical manifestations were malaise (84.8%), fever (54.4%), and vascular bruits (54.4%). Children under 10 years had a lower proportion of girls ( P = 0.016), lower erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein, and platelet levels ( P < 0.05), ITAS.A scores (8.9 ± 4.3 vs 12.0 ± 4.4, P = 0.005), required more surgical interventions at diagnosis (32% vs 7.4%, P = 0.008) compared to adolescents. At follow-up, 34.4% of patients had persistent vascular imaging activity despite normalized laboratory parameters. Biological drugs were used in 50.6% of patients. Three patients died, all due to postoperative complications. This pioneer Russian cohort study of childhood-onset TA reveals a unique clinical phenotype. Younger children show lower levels of inflammation than adolescents, yet they still require more surgical intervention.

items.title: Left Ventricular Myocardial Deformation Abnormalities in Ankylosing Spondylitis (Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis): Association With Disease Severity Assessed by Two-Dimensional Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS), also termed radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA) under current Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) nomenclature, is a chronic inflammatory disorder associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular involvement, including subclinical myocardial dysfunction. Conventional echocardiography often fails to detect early myocardial abnormalities despite preserved left ventricular systolic function. Two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) enables sensitive assessment of myocardial deformation through global longitudinal strain (GLS), facilitating the early detection of subclinical cardiac involvement. This study aimed to evaluate left ventricular myocardial deformation in patients with AS using 2D-STE and investigate its relationship with disease severity and duration. This cross-sectional observational study included 35 patients with AS diagnosed according to the Modified New York criteria. All participants underwent comprehensive clinical evaluation, laboratory investigations, conventional transthoracic echocardiography, and 2D-STE. Disease activity was assessed using the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) and Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS). Radiographic disease severity was determined using the modified New York sacroiliitis grading system. Correlations between myocardial deformation parameters, radiographic severity, and disease duration were analyzed using Pearson's correlation coefficient. The study population had a mean age of 33.9 ± 7.3 years, and 68.6% were male. Conventional echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function, with a mean left ventricular ejection fraction of 65.6±5.0%. The mean GLS was -17.92±4.80%. Radiographic sacroiliitis grade demonstrated a significant positive correlation with global longitudinal strain (r = 0.345, P = 0.046), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (r = 0.455, P = 0.008), and apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (r = 0.392, P = 0.022), whereas no significant association was observed with apical three-chamber strain, aortic root diameter, or valvular abnormalities. Disease duration showed a moderate negative correlation with GLS (r = -0.544, P = 0.001), indicating greater impairment of myocardial deformation in patients with longer-standing disease. Patients with AS demonstrated evidence of subclinical left ventricular myocardial dysfunction despite preserved conventional systolic function. Greater radiographic disease severity and longer disease duration were significantly associated with impaired myocardial deformation assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography. These findings support the potential role of GLS as a sensitive imaging biomarker for the early detection of cardiac involvement in AS and highlight the importance of cardiovascular surveillance in patients with advanced or longstanding disease.

items.title: Proinflammatory strains of Mediterraneibacter gnavus are enriched during spondyloarthritis and bolster disease severity in animal model.
items.abstract: Spondyloarthritis (SpA) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatism with osteoarticular and extra‑articular manifestations. Intestinal dysbiosis has been implicated in SpA, notably the expansion of Mediterraneibacter gnavus (MG), a gram-positive coccus associated with several inflammatory disorders. We aimed to determine whether distinct MG strains were associated with SpA and contributed to disease pathogenesis. MG strains from patients with SpA and healthy controls (HCs) were identified based on metagenomic analysis, isolated and whole‑genome sequenced. Pathogenicity of selected strains was compared by mono-associating curdlan-treated germ‑free SpA-prone SKG mice. Putative strain selection under inflammatory pressure was examined by culturing MG in the presence of nitric oxide (NO). Functional effects were assessed by exposing monocytes from patients with SpA to MGstrains. Phylogenetic analysis separated MG strains into 3 main clades/subclades, using both metagenomic data and sequencing of 46 MG strains (39 from SpA and 7 from HCs). SpA-derived strains were significantly enriched in 2 clades/subclades, whereas the third clade was dominated by strains from HCs, suggesting clade-specific disease association. MG-mono-association of curdlan-treated SKG mice induced SpA, in which SpA-derived strains induced stronger colonic inflammation and arthritis. Consistently, MG DNA of these strains persisted in the inflamed colonic submucosa and SpA-derived strains showed enhanced resistance to NO. In vitro SpA-derived strains were enriched in toxic and proinflammatory properties. SpA is associated with a distinct repertoire of MG strains characterised by increased adaptability to inflammatory stress and heightened proinflammatory and toxic potential. These findings establish a link between strain‑level microbial diversity and disease susceptibility.

items.title: Title: Impact of Coexisting Gout on Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Data from the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative (OBRI).
items.abstract: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with coexisting gout in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluate whether concomitant gout is associated with worse RA disease activity. We conducted a retrospective study of RA patients enrolled in the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative, a multicentre real-world cohort across Ontario, Canada. Coexisting gout was defined by patient- or physician-reported diagnosis or xanthine oxidase inhibitor use. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with coexisting gout and the impact of gout on oral glucocorticoid (GC) use. The association between baseline gout and longitudinal RA disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index, CDAI ≤10) was examined using mixed-effects logistic regression at 24-months, adjusting for prespecified confounders. Among 3,703 RA patients, 113 (3.1%) had coexisting gout with mean (SD) age of 66.1 (8.7) years and 52.2% were female. Coexisting gout was associated with older age (OR 1.05 per year), obesity (OR 1.67), cardiovascular disease or hypertension (OR 1.95) and diuretic use (OR 1.68), while female sex was inversely associated (OR 0.31). CDAI scores were similar between patients with and without gout at baseline (18.3±12.5 vs 20.2±13.5) and at 12-months (10.9±9.8 vs 11.0±10.4). After adjustment, baseline coexisting gout was neither significantly associated with oral GC use at 12-months (OR 1.73, 95% CI: 0.96-3.13) or the attainment of CDAI low disease activity/remission by 24-months (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 0.72-1.97). In this large real-world RA cohort, coexisting gout was uncommon and associated with traditional gout risk factors but did not statistically influence oral GC use or RA treatment target attainment.

items.title: Folate-decorated nanoparticles deliver bulleyaconitine A to inflammatory macrophages for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by synovial inflammatory cell infiltration and progressive joint erosion. Macrophages undergo a pathological shift toward an M1 pro-inflammatory phenotype, which plays a critical role in the progression of the disease. Modulation of M1 macrophages may be a promising therapeutic strategy. Herein, we developed folic acid-functionalized PLGA nanoparticles (FA-PLGA NPs) for targeted delivery of an anti-inflammatory natural compound, bulleyaconitine A (BLA), into M1 macrophages. The nanoparticles exhibited a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 151.91 ± 5.41 nm with a polydispersity index of 0.153 ± 0.016, a negative zeta potential (-13.50 ± 0.82 mV), a high encapsulation efficiency of 90.0%, and excellent colloidal stability. In vitro, FA-PLGA NPs were efficiently internalized by M1-polarized RAW264.7 macrophages via folate receptor-mediated endocytosis, and the uptake level was 7.79-fold higher than non-targeted NPs. Exposure to the NPs significantly reduced the population of CD86-positive M1 cells and decreased iNOS expression while increasing Arg-1 expression. Transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of pro-inflammatory and tissue-destructive pathways and upregulation of myeloid differentiation and immune regulation genes. In an adjuvant-induced arthritis rat model, FA-PLGA NPs treatment resulted in significant alleviation of paw swelling, joint destruction, and cartilage proteoglycan loss, as well as a decrease in the levels of serum IL-6 and TNF-α. Encouragingly, the nanoparticle formulation exhibited favorable in vivo safety, with no observable adverse effects on major organs. Collectively, FA‑PLGA NPs effectively modulated M1 macrophages and achieved potent anti‑arthritic efficacy with improved safety, demonstrating their potential as a nanotherapeutic for RA management.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in axial spondyloarthritis imaging: a review of current evidence.
items.abstract: The diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) remains challenging and is frequently delayed. Imaging is central to diagnosis, but relevant inflammatory and structural abnormalities may be subtle, heterogeneous, or overlap with findings related to mechanical stress, anatomical variation, and degeneration. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is therefore being investigated to support image interpretation, lesion detection, quantification, and standardized assessment. We synthesize evidence from 12 studies applying convolutional neural networks and related architectures to magnetic resonance imaging and radiographs, automate imaging scores, and combine imaging-derived information with clinical variables. Several models achieved performance comparable to experienced human readers, including during external validation. However, performance may decline in heterogeneous real-world populations for study-specific reasons not explained solely by scanner or protocol differences. No AI tool currently has regulatory clearance for autonomous use in axSpA, and applications remain largely confined to research and clinical trials.

items.title: Quality of life in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: positive associations with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and corticosteroid and cyclophosphamide treatment-cross-sectional study in northwestern Poland.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) - chronic autoimmune disease affecting health-related quality of life (QoL). To estimate the associations between QoL and age, disease activity, education level, and treatment in patients with SLE. We studied 200 SLE patients. Data collected: sex, age, disease duration, socioeconomic status, disease activity, and treatment. QoL was assessed using the Lupus Quality of Life Questionnaire (LupusQoL), 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), and Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ). Younger patients reported better QoL (all p < 0.001). Disease duration correlated positively with pain (p = 0.002) and role limitations due to physical health (p = 0.03) in the SF-36. Low SLEDAI correlated positively with QoL in most of the domains assessed by the LupusQoL (all p < 0.05), despite physical health, pain and burden to others, and intimate relationships (all p > 0.05). The use of CS improved physical health (p = 0.01) and physical functioning (p = 0.03) in the LupusQoL and SF-36, respectively. Intravenous cyclophosphamide improved physical health (p = 0.01), oral cyclophosphamide improved intimate relationships (p = 0.003) in the LupusQoL. Secondary and higher education correlated positively with planning (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005, respectively) and intimate relationships (p = 0.0001 and p = 0.0002, respectively) in the LupusQoL and with role limitations due to emotional problems (p = 0.01 and p = 0.007, respectively) in the SF-36. QoL assessment in patients with SLE was positively associated with younger age, higher education, low disease activity, and treatment.

items.title: Clinical patterns and major organ involvement in Behçet's syndrome: a latent class analysis of a regional cohort.
items.abstract: Behçet's syndrome is a heterogeneous disease with diverse patterns of organ involvement. We aimed to identify clinical subgroups using latent class analysis and evaluate clinical characteristics and treatment patterns across the identified subgroups and sex. We retrospectively evaluated 136 patients fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease. Latent class analysis (LCA) based on six clinical indicators was used to identify clinical subgroups. Clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, and current treatments were compared between the identified latent classes and by sex. Major organ involvement occurred in 79 patients (58.1%). Among the standard LCA models, the two-class solution had the lowest BIC. Class 1 (40.4%) was characterized by absence of pathergy positivity and a very low probability of papulopustular lesions (1.3%), but a higher probability of ocular involvement (60.0%). Class 2 (59.6%) showed high probabilities of pathergy positivity (90.7%) and papulopustular lesions (57.7%). Major organ involvement was more frequent in Class 1 than in Class 2 (70.9% vs. 49.4%, p = 0.020). Male patients had significantly higher rates of ocular (52.7% vs. 35.5%, p = 0.044), vascular (28.4% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.003), and major organ involvement (73.0% vs. 40.3%, p < 0.001), as well as current anti-TNF therapy (23.0% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.019), than female patients. Patients with major organ involvement had significantly lower rates of genital ulcer history (51.9% vs. 84.2%, p < 0.001), pathergy positivity (45.6% vs. 70.2%, p = 0.004), and joint involvement (11.4% vs. 28.1%, p = 0.013). The BIC-selected solution identified two main patient groups, but the class structure was highly sensitive to indicator selection. Overall, our findings support exploratory clinical patterns rather than fixed Behçet phenotypes, with major organ involvement being significantly more frequent among men.

items.title: Real-world outcomes of interleukin-17 inhibitors in familial Mediterranean fever-associated inflammatory conditions: a retrospective study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the real-world effects of interleukin-17 (IL-17) inhibitors on familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) activity and associated immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs). We retrospectively evaluated 16 patients with FMF who received IL-17 inhibitors primarily for coexisting IMIDs between 2015 and 2026. FMF attack frequency, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, spondyloarthritis activity indices, treatment duration, discontinuation reasons, and adverse events were assessed. Among 13 patients with available FMF activity data, attack frequency remained unchanged in 9 (69%), increased in 3 (23%), and decreased in 1 (8%). CRP levels did not significantly improve. In six patients with FMF-spondyloarthritis overlap and available 3-month data, BASDAI and ASDAS-CRP showed improvement. IL-17 inhibitor therapy was discontinued in 14 patients, most commonly because of inadequate control of the associated IMID. IL-17 inhibition did not consistently improve core FMF activity in this highly selected, treatment-refractory cohort, although some domain-specific benefit was observed in spondyloarthritis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective controlled studies. Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an inherited inflammatory disease that causes repeated attacks of fever, abdominal or chest pain, and joint inflammation. Some people with FMF also develop other inflammatory conditions, such as spondyloarthritis, psoriasis, or hidradenitis suppurativa. IL-17 inhibitors are treatments commonly used for some of these conditions, but little is known about how they affect FMF itself.We reviewed the medical records of 16 people with FMF who received an IL-17 inhibitor, mainly to treat an inflammatory condition occurring alongside FMF rather than FMF itself. We assessed FMF attack frequency, blood markers of inflammation, treatment duration, reasons for stopping treatment, and, when available, measures of spondyloarthritis activity.IL-17 inhibitor treatment did not consistently reduce FMF attacks or blood inflammation levels. Some patients with spondyloarthritis showed improvement in joint and spine-related disease activity, but these results were based on only a small number of patients. Most patients had already received several other treatments, and IL-17 inhibitors were stopped in many patients because of limited benefit.These findings suggest that IL-17 inhibitors may help some coexisting inflammatory conditions but may not be sufficient to control FMF itself. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings and identify which patients are most likely to benefit.

items.title: Minimizing delays in systemic lupus erythematosus diagnosis: a proposed diagnostic algorithm from symptom onset to rheumatology referral.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic, multisystem autoimmune disease with heterogeneous clinical manifestations that complicate recognition and delay diagnosis, contributing to substantial clinical, emotional, and socioeconomic burden. SLE mainly affects women (female:male ratio ≈ 9:1) during their reproductive years. It should be identified early in primary care to shorten the time to specialist referral. An expert working group was formed to discuss strategies to accelerate SLE recognition and referral in Croatia. It was composed of five rheumatologists/clinical immunologists from tertiary centers with experience in treating SLE patients. They searched Medline/PubMed for articles on diagnostic delay in SLE. During three meetings, local-specific barriers were identified, and a women-specific diagnostic algorithm and educational plan for primary care physicians (PCPs) were developed. Key barriers included limited SLE awareness among PCPs, nonspecific and multiorgan presentations, absence of specific diagnostic tests, reliance on classification criteria, insufficient training and referral protocols, workforce overload, and shortages of rheumatologists/immunologists, leading to multiple unnecessary referrals before specialist assessment. The group developed an expert proposal aimed at reducing diagnostic delays in patients with suspected SLE. Patients should be promptly referred to a rheumatologist/immunologist when ≥1 clinical symptom (arthralgia/myalgia/malar rash/photosensitivity/alopecia/oral ulceration/fatigue/fever) is accompanied by elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and ≥1 laboratory abnormality (urinary abnormalities, hypocomplementemia, or cytopenias). The proposed training strategy consists of interactive workshops (≤10 PCPs) using clinical cases, organized through regional primary care managers. A pilot study is planned in which trained PCPs would apply the algorithm to their patients to evaluate its impact on diagnostic delay.

items.title: JAK inhibitor retention and adverse event-related discontinuation in elderly patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a real-world cohort study.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in elderly patients poses management challenges due to comorbidities and polypharmacy. JAK inhibitors offer oral-administration advantages, but their safety in the elderly remains uncertain. We compared the retention and discontinuation reasons of JAK inhibitors in patients with RA who initiated therapy at age ≥ 65 versus < 65 years in a real-world setting. We included 317 patients with RA treated with JAK inhibitors at a single tertiary center (2000-2025), classified as ≥ 65 years (H65Y, n = 97) or < 65 years (L65Y, n = 220). The outcomes were retention and cause-specific discontinuation, with a single primary reason per patient. Drug retention was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis and compared using the log-rank test; factors associated with discontinuation were assessed by multivariable Cox regression. No statistically significant difference in overall retention was detected between the groups (HR [95% CI] 1.18 [0.419, 1.714], log-rank p = 0.680). However, discontinuation due to adverse effects was significantly more frequent in the H65Y group (10/20 [50.0%] vs. 6/52 [11.5%]). No cardiovascular- or malignancy-related discontinuations were observed in the H65Y group; however, given the limited cohort size and follow-up, the study was underpowered to detect these infrequent outcomes. Concomitant methotrexate (HR 2.94) or glucocorticoid (HR 3.73) use was associated with subsequent discontinuation. Herpes zoster incidence was significantly higher in the H65Y group (adjusted HR 1.94 [95% CI] 1.02-3.71; p = 0.044), with approximately half of the cases occurring within the first treatment year. No statistically significant difference in JAK inhibitor retention between the elderly and younger groups was detected. Because this study assessed reasons for discontinuation rather than systematically ascertained safety events, it does not permit conclusions regarding cardiovascular or malignancy safety. Herpes zoster, particularly during the early treatment phase, warrants heightened vigilance in elderly patients initiating JAK inhibitor therapy. Key Points • No significant difference in JAK inhibitor retention between the elderly and younger groups was detected. • As only the primary reason for discontinuation was recorded, this study does not assess cardiovascular or malignancy safety; its findings pertain to drug retention and adverse event-related discontinuation. • Herpes zoster risk was significantly higher in elderly patients, mostly within the first treatment year, warranting early vigilance.

items.title: Association between baseline systemic immune-inflammation index and subsequent stroke in ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is reportedly an effective predictor of poor outcomes in malignancies and inflammatory diseases. Therefore, this study investigated the association between baseline SII and subsequent stroke in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV). We selected 339 immunosuppressive drug-naïve patients newly diagnosed with AAV from an observational AAV cohort and retrospectively reviewed their medical records. The baseline Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS) was reviewed, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were recorded. Baseline SII was calculated thus: SII = neutrophil count × platelet count/lymphocyte count. Subsequent stroke was defined as ischaemic or haemorrhagic stroke that occurred after diagnosis. The 339 AAV patients had a median age of 61.0 years; the majority were women. The median baseline BVAS and SII were 12.0 and 1229.9, respectively. Of the 339 patients, 20 (5.9%) experienced a subsequent stroke. Baseline SII was significantly correlated with ESR (r = 0.361) and CRP levels (r = 0.485). Baseline SII (standardised β 0.117) was independently correlated with BVAS, as seen on multivariable linear regression analysis. Baseline SII showed modest discrimination for subsequent stroke (AUC 0.662, 95% CI 0.532-0.793), and a cohort-derived cutoff of 2390.5 was identified. Patients with baseline SII ≥ 2390.5 and those in the upper half of baseline SII showed significantly lower cumulative stroke-free survival rates. However, baseline SII was not independently associated with subsequent stroke in the primary multivariable Cox analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate an association between baseline SII and subsequent stroke in patients with AAV. Further studies are required to establish its independent and incremental prognostic value. Key Points • Baseline SII was significantly correlated with cross-sectional BVAS, ESR, and CRP levels. • Individuals with baseline SII ≥ 2390.5 and those with the upper half of baseline SII showed significantly reduced cumulative stroke-free survival rates compared to those without. • Higher baseline SII was associated with subsequent stroke in patients with AAV; however, its independent and incremental prognostic value remains to be established.

items.title: Prevalence of depression and anxiety among patients with Behçet's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a chronic multisystemic vasculitis associated with significant physical and psychological morbidity, including depression and anxiety. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of depression and anxiety among BD patients and to examine variations by assessment tools and geographic regions. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted up to April 2025. Data were extracted and quality-assessed using standardized tools, and pooled prevalence rates were calculated via random-effects meta-analysis. A total of 17 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 16 contributed to the meta-analysis of depression and 11 to the meta-analysis of anxiety among patients with BD. The results revealed a high pooled prevalence of depression at 47.44% (95% CI: 34.09-60.97%) and anxiety at 48.48% (95% CI: 35.40-61.67%), both with substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%). Depression prevalence varied significantly by diagnostic instrument, with PHQ-9 and HADS reporting higher rates compared to DSM-IV and MINI. Geographic differences were marked, with Egypt showing the highest prevalence for both depression (88.83%) and anxiety (92.00%), while France reported the lowest prevalence for depression (5.00%) and Brazil reported the lowest for anxiety (29.31%). No publication bias was detected. The findings underscore a high burden of mental health comorbidities in BD, with pooled prevalence rates of 47.44% for depression and 48.48% for anxiety, reflecting significant psychological morbidity. Geographic disparities, suggest cultural, healthcare, or socioeconomic moderators requiring further investigation. These results advocate for integrating routine mental health screening into BD management to address unmet psychiatric needs in this population.

items.title: Screening of nearly equivalent component groups and mechanism investigation of Si Miao San for treating rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic disease involving synovitis, cartilage damage, and bone erosion. Si Miao San (SMS), a traditional Chinese formula, shows anti‑RA potential, but its complex composition and mechanisms remain unclear. We developed a novel systems pharmacology strategy combining node importance scoring and Component Contribution Weight (CCW) modeling to identify the nearly equivalent component group (NECG) from SMS. A functional action space was constructed by integrating SMS targets with RA‑related pathogenic genes, and functional proteins were selected via the node importance algorithm. The NECG was validated through molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro experiments in RAW264.7 macrophages and fibroblast‑like synoviocytes (FLSs). The NECG covered 100% of enriched pathways and 88.76% of GO terms from reference targets. From 194 initial components, 31 compounds were selected as NECG members, enriching 171 pathways and covering 78.57% of pathogenic gene‑associated pathways. KEGG analysis highlighted the PI3K‑Akt pathway as a key mediator. Four representative components-auraptene, jatrorrhizine, THB, and myristic acid-showed stable binding to their targets in docking and dynamics simulations. This study presents a reliable systems pharmacology model that effectively elucidates the active components and mechanism of SMS against RA, offering an integrative framework for modernizing TCM formula research.

items.title: ANCA-negative eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis diagnosed via external auditory canal biopsy: A case report.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an uncommon systemic vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. The diagnosis of ANCA-negative EGPA may be challenging because serological findings are often non-specific, making histopathological confirmation important. We report a case of ANCA-negative EGPA diagnosed by biopsy of the external auditory canal, an uncommon but readily accessible site of disease involvement. A 22-year-old Mongolian woman presented with progressive chest tightness and dyspnea. Her medical history was notable for asthma and nasal polyps. She also reported bilateral ear fullness and tinnitus. Laboratory investigations demonstrated marked eosinophilia (35.8% of leukocytes), while ANCA testing was negative. Otoscopic examination revealed inflammatory changes in the left external auditory canal, and biopsy was subsequently performed. Histopathological examination showed vasculitis with prominent eosinophilic infiltration, supporting the diagnosis of EGPA. Treatment with systemic corticosteroids resulted in rapid clinical improvement. At three-month follow-up, eosinophil counts had normalized and no evidence of disease progression was observed. This case highlights the potential diagnostic value of external auditory canal biopsy in patients with suspected ANCA-negative EGPA. Otologic manifestations may provide accessible sites for tissue sampling when histological confirmation is required. Careful otologic examination should therefore be considered during the evaluation of patients with suspected EGPA.

items.title: Case Report: Spinal cord herniation associated with ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: Spinal cord herniation (SCH) is a rare clinical entity characterized by the ventral displacement of the spinal cord through a dural defect. While often classified as idiopathic, SCH associated with ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is exceedingly rare. The pathogenesis in such cases remains unclear, and treatment strategies are not well standardized. Herein, we report a series of four patients with long-standing ankylosing spondylitis who presented with SCH between August 2018 and August 2021. All patients exhibited severe thoracolumbar kyphosis and restricted spinal mobility. Uniquely, the herniations occurred at the vertebral body level rather than the disc level, and one patient presented with rare multilevel herniations. Two patients underwent pedicle subtraction osteotomy (PSO) with spinal fusion. In both surgical cases, direct dural repair was avoided; stabilization was achieved through indirect cord relaxation via spinal column shortening. Postoperative imaging showed successful kyphosis correction and stabilization of the herniation. SCH in patients with AS is a distinct entity secondary to inflammatory and biomechanical changes. PSO with fusion is a viable surgical option that addresses both deformity and cord tethering through an indirect mechanism.

items.title: Joint disease in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical manifestations, immunopathology, and treatment.
items.abstract: Joint involvement affects the majority of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and is consistently ranked among the manifestations with the largest impact on daily function, yet lupus synovium remains one of the least interrogated major target tissues in this disease. The primary literature on lupus synovial tissue rests mainly on two datasets, neither generated by single-cell transcriptomic or mass cytometric methods, and what they describe is a relatively pauci-immune and myeloid-dominated compartment carrying an interferon-inducible transcriptional signature in situ , without the ectopic germinal centers and expanded pathogenic fibroblast populations that characterize rheumatoid synovitis. The cell populations now central to systemic lupus biology, among them T peripheral helper cells and double-negative 2 B cells, have never been examined in lupus synovial tissue, so that every cellular account of this compartment remains an extrapolation from rheumatoid arthritis. Recent large-cohort data nevertheless indicate that lupus arthropathy is not a single entity, since non-deforming arthritis and Jaccoud's arthropathy are both associated with a high type I interferon signature whereas arthritis with clinically irreducible deformity is interferon-low, although whether these represent distinct biological trajectories or successive stages of a single process remains to be established. This heterogeneity is invisible to the instruments used in practice, because the composite indices that grade disease activity and determine eligibility for advanced therapy depend on the detection of joint swelling at the bedside, while musculoskeletal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging independently demonstrate inflammation in approximately half of patients whose joints appear clinically unremarkable, together with erosive change in patients who lack anti-citrullinated protein antibodies. Misclassification of articular disease is therefore systematic and bidirectional, and the same failure has propagated into drug development, where no recent registrational program has used imaging to define articular response, even though the proportion of patients failing on articular endpoints lies between roughly a third and a half. This review synthesizes the immunopathological, biomarker, imaging and therapeutic literatures, and argues that single-cell interrogation of the lupus synovium, a lupus-specific imaging scoring system and a validated imaging-anchored articular outcome measure are the necessary next steps if this manifestation is to be treated with the precision now applied to lupus nephritis.

items.title: Spatial multiomics identifies rheumatoid arthritis synovial niches and de-novo laminar histological patterns of fibroblasts subtypes.
items.abstract: Spatial omic technologies provide insight into molecular architecture and spatial cellular organization within tissue. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), single-cell RNA sequencing and low-resolution spatial transcriptomics have advanced the understanding of synovial biology. However, single-cell spatial resolution using multiple spatial platforms to comprehensively map the immune and stromal cell organization as well as topographical cellular interactions in the RA synovium remain limited. We integrated single-cell and bulk spatial transcriptomics (CosMx and Xenium, and Visium, respectively) as well as spatial LC/MS proteomics and a multiplex immunohistochemical protein panel in the histological evaluation of a non-clinical cohort of six RA, three osteoarthritis (OA) and three healthy (NH) arthroscopic synovial biopsies. The histopathological observations were integrated with Xenium-based spatial computational analyses in the RA and NH synovium to define fibroblast organization and spatial relationships in RA compared to the NH synovium. Cross-platform comparisons demonstrated a strong concordance in cellular composition and microanatomical localization and highlighted the strengths of each technology, with single-cell spatial analysis providing higher cellular resolution, but reduced molecular depth. Comparison of single-cell spatial transcriptomics and LC/MS proteomics also demonstrated concordance, but revealed region-specific expression of fibroblast-associated genes and proteins. Spatial mapping in our large biopsies identified a previously unrecognized laminar organization of up to nine fibroblast subtypes spanning the lining and sublining regions of RA synovium, distinct from NH. Spatial computational pathology analyses showed that specific fibroblast subtypes preferentially localized within lymphoid (CD74+ and CXCL12+), vascular (NOTCH3+ and mural) and stromal (POSTN+, DKK3+ and CD34+) niches. Pathway enrichment analyses further implicated specific biological functions to the fibroblast subtypes that were linked to their microenvironment. This multimodal spatial molecular pathology study indicates that in RA, fibroblast subtypes expand, spatially reorganize, and establish specialized tissue niches that likely contribute to disease pathogenesis. These findings provide a high-resolution spatial framework and support future spatial multiomics studies aimed at identifying fibroblast ecotypes in the context of treatment naïve, treatment-responsive and treatment-refractory RA patients to identify tissue-level spatial signatures associated with inadequate response to treatments.

items.title: TNF-driven intracellular complement factor H-NF-κB feed-forward loop amplifies inflammatory mediator production in rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines; fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) are central effector cells that integrate these signals to produce pathogenic mediators. Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) is a major upstream driver of coordinated inflammatory mediator induction in FLS; however, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined, particularly intracellular feed-forward amplification sustaining and enhancing TNF-driven transcriptional outputs. Complement factor H (FH; gene CFH), a Sushi domain-only complement regulator, is elevated in RA serum. FH is regarded as an extracellular inhibitor of complement activation; however, its potential intracellular expression and functions in FLS have not been explored. We aimed to investigate intracellular FH expression and function using an in vitro transcribed messenger RNA (IVT mRNA)-based approach. FH expression in sera, synovial tissues, and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting. To examine intracellular FH function, FLS were transfected with CFH-encoding IVT mRNA to express FH intracellularly, followed by next-generation sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, ELISA, phosphorylation assays, and pathway inhibition. Interactions between TNF-driven signaling and intracellular FH were evaluated using TNF- and/or FH-neutralizing antibodies, with or without CFH-targeting small interfering RNA (siRNA). FH was highly expressed in RA synovium and predominantly localized intracellularly in FLS. To assess intracellular FH function, FLS were transfected with CFH-encoding IVT mRNA, which induced the coordinated upregulation of RA-relevant mediators, including granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), interleukin (IL)-8, IL-6, and multiple chemokines. Mechanistically, intracellular FH activated nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling, promoting receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 2 (RIPK2) phosphorylation and p65 nuclear translocation, and the competitive nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain 2 (NOD2) antagonist suppressed FH-driven gene induction. TNF and intracellular FH additively enhanced pathogenic mediator production. CFH-targeting siRNA attenuated TNF-induced cytokine and chemokine expression; blockade of extracellular FH had no detectable effect. Combined TNF neutralization and CFH knockdown produced more effective suppression of cytokine induction than either intervention alone. Intracellular FH is a previously unrecognized amplifier of TNF-driven inflammation in RA-FLS via a NOD2/RIPK2/NF-κB axis, establishing a feed-forward loop boosting pathogenic mediator production. Dual targeting of TNF and intracellular FH may represent a therapeutic strategy to suppress synovial inflammation more effectively.
